reason: Agent W (council-remediation-2026-07-20) source-audit fixes a substantive content error left untouched by the prior Batch 094 metadata-only edit. The linked question's marked-correct option (b 'one full additional term only') is correct under RA 9266 Section 6, but the rationale 'correct' string states 'limiting maximum tenure to 6 years for Chairman and 4 years for Members.' The 4-year ceiling for Members is wrong: under Section 6, reappointment is for 'one full term of three (3) years' applied uniformly, so for the FIRST Board a Member initially serving 2 years can be reappointed for a full 3-year term (5 years max), and a Member initially serving 1 year can be reappointed for a full 3-year term (4 years max). The Member ceiling is therefore 5 years, not 4. After the first Board's staggered cycle has passed, every regular member serves 3+3=6 years max. The Batch 094 edit refreshed only code_citation and explanation metadata without touching the wrong rationale. This edit rewrites the rationale 'correct' string so the maximum-tenure statement is source-accurate.

source_audit_support.local_source_safe_action: corrected rationale 'correct' string which previously understated Member maximum tenure (4 years); replaced with source-accurate 5-year ceiling for the longer-serving first Board member and 6-year ceiling for all subsequent members

proposed.text: Under Section 6, how many times may a PRBoA member be reappointed after their initial term?

rationale.a: Unlimited reappointments would create indefinite tenure contrary to democratic rotation principles.
rationale.c: Two additional terms would exceed the single-reappointment ceiling that Section 6 sets.
rationale.d: Reappointment is allowed by Section 6, but limited to one additional term.
rationale.correct: Section 6 states that each member of the Board may be reappointed for one full term of three (3) years. The ceiling is therefore one reappointment. Because Section 6 also prescribes staggered initial terms for the first Board (Chairman 3 years, one Member 2 years, the other Member 1 year), the resulting maximum tenures on the first Board are 6 years for the Chairman, 5 years for the Member with a 2-year initial term, and 4 years for the Member with a 1-year initial term. Once the staggered cycle has passed, every member serves a 3-year initial term and may be reappointed for a further 3 years, so the regular maximum tenure is 6 years.
rationale.takeaway: The single-reappointment limit of one full 3-year term prevents entrenched power while ensuring sufficient tenure for policy continuity and expertise deployment.

proposed.explanation: The original rationale incorrectly stated 'limiting maximum tenure to 6 years for Chairman and 4 years for Members.' Section 6 fixes the reappointment at one full 3-year term regardless of the member's initial term, so the maximum tenure for the longer-serving first Board Member is 5 years (2+3), not 4.
